subject.title: fix: block unsafe workspace dotenv controls [AI]

question: Should workspace `.env` files be prevented from setting the newly listed provider, channel, relay, and runtime-toggle controls under this precise policy boundary?
rationale: This is an intentional trust-boundary and compatibility decision: the patch changes which existing repository-local variables are ignored, and the protected `maintainer` label requires explicit human handling.

options.title: Approve the proposed boundary
options.body: Accept the expanded workspace-only blocklist once a runtime transcript proves trusted shell and global dotenv values still take precedence.

options.title: Narrow the protected controls
options.body: Retain only individually confirmed operator-owned controls if maintainers do not want pattern-based blocking for workspace variables.

options.title: Pause for a broader policy design
options.body: Defer this PR if the repository needs a documented classification of trusted versus project-local dotenv controls before expanding the denylist.

recommendation.title: Approve the proposed boundary
recommendation.body: Accept the expanded workspace-only blocklist once a runtime transcript proves trusted shell and global dotenv values still take precedence.

likelyOwner.reason: No attributable current-main history was available in the read-only review materials; a dotenv/runtime owner should make the trust-policy call.
